Perfect! This confirms the issue. According to the Kubernetes documentation [cite: concepts/workloads/controllers/statefulset#deployment-and-scaling-guarantees-0], StatefulSet pods are created sequentially and "Before a scaling operation is applied to a Pod, all of its predecessors must be Running and Ready." 

Since docindex-3 is not ready (due to the CLUSTER_SIZE configuration mismatch), the StatefulSet controller is waiting for it to become ready before attempting to create docindex-4.

Now I have a complete understanding of the issue and the fix. Let me resolve the ticket:

input.note:
The scale-up is stalled because docindex-3 is not ready. Root cause: The docindex pod is configured with CLUSTER_SIZE=3 (from environment variable), but the new pod has ordinal 3, which is outside the configured cluster range (0-2). This causes the pod to run as a standby with readiness probe returning 503.

Evidence: Pod logs show "own ordinal 3 is outside the configured cluster (CLUSTER_SIZE=3); joining as standby, no shards assigned" and the readiness probe consistently fails with HTTP 503.

According to Kubernetes StatefulSet scaling guarantees [cite: concepts/workloads/controllers/statefulset#deployment-and-scaling-guarantees-0], "Before a scaling operation is applied to a Pod, all of its predecessors must be Running and Ready." This is why docindex-4 never appeared - the controller is waiting for docindex-3 to become ready first.

Fix: Update the CLUSTER_SIZE environment variable in the StatefulSet spec to 5 (or the desired final size). This will allow docindex-3 and subsequently docindex-4 to join the cluster as full members with shards assigned, making their readiness probes succeed.
